PKO Dziennik 15 Jan: MPC pause ('to sit out the frost') firmed PLN slightly and lifted SPW yields +1/+7bp on 14 Jan; Glapinski's 15:00 conference and geopolitics to set tone; revised Dec CPI expected at 2.4% y/y.

PAP morning: ING notes the MPC statement was terse and the conference will refresh the outlook; Millennium says a cautious Glapinski tone supporting its March-cut call could lift short-term market rates.

GUS final Dec CPI 2.4% y/y, 0.0% m/m (= flash 2.4/0.0; consensus 2.4% per PKO calendar); Nov 2.5%. 2025 average 3.6%. Goods 1.3% y/y, services 5.2%; food & non-alc. bev. 2.4%; alcohol & tobacco 7.9%; housing & energy 4.1%; transport -3.2%; health 4.7%; communication 3.6%; recreation 1.9%; education 6.1%; restaurants & hotels 5.2%; clothing -2.2%.

ING (A. Antoniak): disinflation trend strong; ref rate to 3.25% by end-2026 in 25bp steps. Bank Pocztowy (M. Kurtek): CPI near 2.0% in Jan-Mar; MPC waits in Feb, resumes cuts in March (April latest), ref rate 3.50% at turn of Q1/Q2 and held there.
BNP Paribas economists: 2026 GDP 3.7%, CPI avg 2.1% (slightly below 2.5% much of the year); two 25bp cuts in 2026 to 3.50%; EURPLN around 4.20 all year.
Alior Bank: 2026 GDP 3.8%; room for 75bp more cuts to 3.25% in H1 2026; potential for further falls in yields limited, especially at the long end.

Post-conference: ING (A. Antoniak) - key message disinflation 'durable'; pause will be short, next 25bp cut in March, ref rate 3.25% by end-2026. Santander/Erste (P. Bielski) - Feb hold (no new CPI data before Feb meeting), cuts in March and May, cycle ends at 3.50%.

Glapinski press conference (from 15:00): would see the terminal ref rate at 3.5% with real rate at least 1-1.5% ('some members see it lower'); must not go too low and then hike quickly; 'still some room, then we stop'. Moves >25bp unlikely ('fine-tuning'). 'I do not exclude February, nor say it will be February; I do not exclude March, nor say it will be March' - March projection is not a 'holy date'; if not Feb could even be April. Dovish majority ('the other bird flies over all MPC members'). Disinflation durable; CPI within 2.5%+/-1pp target band all 2026 per current NBP projections (stabilisation to year-end); wage growth (~7%) to keep slowing; cheap Chinese imports disinflationary. Risks: demand pressure (KPO 'booster' until end-2027), wages, fiscal deficit/debt. NBP to raise gold to 700t from ~550t.
MoF: 16 Jan T-bill auction offer - 36-week bills, PLN 2-4bn (as in the January plan).

gpwb.integrity_flag: DOUBT: the PDF now served was generated 2 Feb 2026 (after the 30 Jan effective date) and the file name carries a trailing underscore (other months, e.g. Portfele_obligacji_2026_10_28.pdf, do not), suggesting a re-upload replacing the 28 Jan original; variants without underscore return 404, so the original could not be compared. Supporting evidence the numbers are as originally published: all TBSP unit changes vs the Dec communique reconcile exactly with MoF sales settled 23 Dec-26 Jan (30-31 Dec OB placements, 9 Jan and 22 Jan auctions + additional sales) and exclude the 28 Jan auction (settled 30 Jan), consistent with 'stan na 27 stycznia'; e.g. PS0131 +11,334,900 = 1,645+350 (30-31 Dec) + 4,886 (9 Jan) + 4,453.9 (22 Jan) m; DS1034 unchanged. Treat as probably-original but unverified.
